name: Variance Analysis and Explanation
title: Variance Analysis and Explanation
answer: Variance analysis and explanation covers the comparison of actual financial and operational results against budgets, forecasts, prior periods, and driver-based plans. It identifies differences in revenue, cost, margin, headcount, and cash, then breaks them into causes such as price, volume, mix, rate, efficiency, foreign exchange, timing, and one-off items. The explanation part turns those numbers into a written narrative for management, the board, auditors, and regulators, stating what moved, by how much, and why. In an AI accounting context, the work also includes flagging unusual variances, ranking them by materiality, and drafting commentary that a human reviewer can edit and approve.

sections.body: Variance analysis and explanation covers the comparison of actual financial and operational results against budgets, forecasts, prior periods, and driver-based plans. It identifies differences in revenue, cost, margin, headcount, and cash, then breaks them into causes such as price, volume, mix, rate, efficiency, foreign exchange, timing, and one-off items. The explanation part turns those numbers into a written narrative for management, the board, auditors, and regulators, stating what moved, by how much, and why. sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on financial data pulled from the general ledger, ERP systems, planning and consolidation tools, data warehouses, and spreadsheets. A typical stack moves actuals and plan data through an extract, transform, and load process into a semantic layer or reporting model that keeps account mappings and hierarchies consistent. Statistical models and large language models may sit on top to decompose variances, detect anomalies, and generate draft explanations. Access controls, versioning, and refresh schedules matter because the same variance can look different depending on the close status and the data cut-off.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Analysts and systems start by reconciling actuals to the plan, confirming the period, currency, and scope, then calculating absolute and percentage variances. They decompose each material variance into drivers, often using volume and rate formulas, mix analysis, or bridge schedules that connect one period to the next. Thresholds and materiality rules decide which variances need investigation, and anomaly detection can surface items that rules alone would miss. Draft explanations are generated from the underlying data and prior commentary, then reviewed for accuracy, causality, and business context before they are published. The method depends on clean mappings, documented assumptions, and a clear separation between what the data shows and what the reviewer concludes.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights, risk, and provenance center on where the numbers came from, who can change them, and how an explanation can be traced back to source records. AI-generated commentary needs an audit trail that links each statement to the ledger, plan, or calculation that supports it, plus version control and review logs. Risks include hallucinated explanations, stale data, hidden model assumptions, and overreliance on a narrative that sounds plausible but is not tied to the accounts. Data rights, confidentiality, and licensing terms for any AI tool also apply, especially when financial data leaves the company's systems. The site's 219 compliance and regulation pages reflect how much of this area is still governed by a mix of accounting standards, audit requirements, and emerging AI rules.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward faster and more continuous variance monitoring, with explanations generated closer to the close and sometimes in real time. Driver-based planning, rolling forecasts, and scenario analysis are making variance work less about a single monthly report and more about a standing process. AI is likely to take on more of the first draft, the anomaly triage, and the link between operational events and financial outcomes, while humans keep responsibility for judgment and sign-off. Expect more emphasis on explainability, audit-ready model documentation, and integration between planning systems and the general ledger. The practical goal is not a fully automated narrative but a shorter path from a variance appearing to a trusted explanation being available.
